outcomes: Labels an unlabeled position better, worse or equal before choosing a move
Does not wait when clearly better and does not raid when clearly worse
Chooses a quiet improving move when the position is level
sources: docs/lessons-positional.md (weaknesses section) and content/skills/POS.PLAN.MODE.json (D2 outcome; the source's advice to give up a hopeless game is not taught here)
items: IBds57-7..12 (labels are engine evaluations at recorded depth [V]; mode names are the author's labelling [I]), IBp3-MODE-11 (shipped)

steps.text: In *Better, worse or equal: the valuation sets the mode* you matched a label to a mode. Now you pick the move itself. A *rule of thumb*: if you are clearly better, a waiting move can give the edge away; if you are clearly worse, a raid (sending a piece deep into the enemy side) gives the opponent a target and a repairing move comes first; if it is level, improve your worst piece. The label comes first.

The mode is a default, not a law, and the engine score is evidence, not a verdict. Count what is different first: material, king safety, activity. When two labels seem possible, say so and choose the move that is safe under both. A level position has no urgent act or defend, so many quiet moves are sound.

steps.title: Worse side: repair or raid?
steps.prompt: Board 1: White is worse. Is the repairing move Rc1 among the best? Board 2 (same position): is the queen raid Qc6 sound? Board 3: is anyone clearly better? Predict each, then check.
For each silent position, what label did you give before you moved? Where did the label and the move disagree, and which one was wrong?

steps.text: **Remember.** Name the valuation first, then pick the move. Clearly better: a waiting move can give the edge away. Clearly worse: repair first, do not raid. Level: improve your worst piece. The mode is a default, not a law. If two labels seem possible, choose a move that is safe under both.
